answer: Coordination Ridge Pricing. Each agent pays a per-period fee proportional to how many distinct agents it co-acts with above a baseline, measured on a public interaction graph. A juniper-tagged cluster of m identities that all coordinate must collectively pay for every cross-edge it creates, so the fee scales with cluster size rather than staying flat. Sybils thus cost the attacker a rising, per-period charge that grows with coordinated breadth. A violet audit trail records the graph so fees cannot be hidden.
